note: Includes proposed reactions and evaluation hypotheses; never provide to the first-pass actor.

profiles.name: Mei
profiles.role: Student founder building an AI prototype
profiles.context: Has a working university project and wants one useful action before applying for support. Has not clarified ownership with the institution.
profiles.knowledge: Comfortable with ordinary web forms. New to grant terminology and commercialisation. Does not know who owns the prototype IP.
profiles.goal: Leave with a specific question and a person or source to consult, without having to invent personal facts.
profiles.preferences: Discreet text input. Short explanations with optional detail. Wants to approve context before it affects the route.
profiles.trust: Treats confident eligibility language as a reason to inspect evidence. Needs to distinguish a suggestion from a requirement.
profiles.behaviour: Reads the first action, then looks for why it fits. Tries a plain-language label before an unfamiliar technical term. Will set a field to Unknown instead of guessing.
profiles.frustration: Repeating the same clarification or being told to apply before knowing the prerequisite.
profiles.disclosure_boundary: No nationality, visa status, institution name or personal identity documents are supplied or inferred.
profiles.surface: Desktop, 1366×768 CSS pixels, text and pointer; keyboard smoke variant.
profiles.autonomy: May edit and inspect. Will not submit an application or contact anyone.
profiles.success: Can explain one next conversation, why it matters, and what remains unknown.
profiles.recruitment_proxy: A consenting first-time student founder with unresolved commercialisation questions; no demographic assumptions.

profiles.name: Arun
profiles.context: Has a laboratory prototype and early customer discussions. Preparing a meeting with a commercialisation adviser.
profiles.knowledge: Strong subject expertise; understands evidence but not every funding pathway. A research milestone is not necessarily a program prerequisite.
profiles.goal: Compare two support routes and take a defensible checklist to the meeting.
profiles.preferences: Tables and a short dependency map, with a textual sequence. Reads the conditions before the summary recommendation.
profiles.trust: Wants a passage behind each material requirement and a distinction between mandatory and suggested sequencing.
profiles.behaviour: Compares the same criterion across columns, opens one factual cell, then asks what is missing. Checks dates when a requirement looks surprising.
profiles.frustration: Attractive diagrams with no evidence; missing comparison cells made to look like negative answers.
profiles.disclosure_boundary: Uses fictional project details; does not share unpublished research or actual institution documents.
profiles.surface: Desktop, 1440×900 CSS pixels, pointer and keyboard.
profiles.autonomy: May mark a personal task and export a local checklist; cannot change shared program requirements.
profiles.success: Can state the first unresolved prerequisite and compare options without treating Unknown as No.
profiles.recruitment_proxy: A consenting research commercialisation participant preparing a support discussion.

profiles.name: Jess
profiles.context: Works on a prototype in Gympie and has a short break to find support that can be used locally or remotely.
profiles.knowledge: Knows the product and location; unfamiliar with ecosystem organisation names. Does not assume a national list is locally useful.
profiles.goal: Find a relevant next contact or honestly learn that local coverage is missing.
profiles.preferences: Phone layout, short answer first, optional push-to-talk when available, visible source links.
profiles.trust: Checks whether the location was understood and whether the option is actually local or remote.
profiles.behaviour: Starts from the visible next-step entry. Skims one screen before opening details. Corrects the town if the transcript is wrong; switches to typing when voice fails.
profiles.frustration: Long generic lists, a lost draft after a network problem, or a transcript sent before it can be checked.
profiles.disclosure_boundary: Only fictional business context. No location permissions or microphone access beyond an explicitly prepared test fixture.
profiles.surface: Mobile viewport 390×844 CSS pixels. This is emulation unless real device/browser details are recorded.
profiles.autonomy: May edit a transcript and choose text instead. Never grants recording permission just to satisfy the test.
profiles.success: Can identify the geographic limitation or a relevant next route and recover without retyping the draft.
profiles.recruitment_proxy: A consenting regional founder who uses a phone for support research; voice preference must be asked, not assumed.

profiles.name: Sam
profiles.relationship: Existing core P4; SB4; later pilot only
profiles.context: Sketching a marketplace payment workflow; has not decided whether the platform or a third party holds customer funds.
profiles.knowledge: Understands product operations but is not acting as a regulatory specialist. Familiar terminology can encourage premature confidence.
profiles.goal: Get useful classification questions and a specialist referral without mistaking the app for launch approval.
profiles.preferences: Precise distinctions and a compact flow diagram. Will ask for a definite answer once.
profiles.trust: Checks which source supports each distinction and whether unknown product details remain visible.
profiles.behaviour: Asks whether registration is enough to launch. If challenged, supplies known facts but leaves custody unknown. Rejects a reversed arrow in a diagram preview.
profiles.frustration: A generic disclaimer with no useful next question, or a confident answer that silently fills in the money flow.
profiles.disclosure_boundary: Synthetic flow diagrams only. No customer records, account numbers or genuine compliance conclusions.
profiles.surface: Desktop 1440×900; later visual-input fixture with an intentionally ambiguous arrow.
profiles.autonomy: May prepare an adviser checklist. Will not open an account, submit a regulatory form or execute a payment.
profiles.success: Can explain the missing product fact and the next specialist question; does not infer permission to operate.
profiles.recruitment_proxy: A consenting payments product builder; legal correctness requires separate qualified review.

profiles.name: Alex
profiles.relationship: Existing core P5; repository-based curator flow
profiles.context: Helping a founder understand conflicting information and reviewing a proposed graph relationship.
profiles.knowledge: Understands provenance and source dates; does not assume two organisations mentioned together are partners.
profiles.goal: Explain a conflict and leave a reproducible correction decision supported by an excerpt.
profiles.preferences: Side-by-side dated evidence and a clear claim record. Comfortable reading repository review artifacts.
profiles.trust: Requires traceable passages, source versions and distinctions between sourced requirements and editorial sequencing.
profiles.behaviour: Opens both conflicting citations, compares effective periods, then checks whether a candidate relationship is entailed by its passage.
profiles.frustration: A confidence score replacing conflicting evidence, or an approval button with no original excerpt.
profiles.disclosure_boundary: Cannot infer operator privileges or access private archives. Public feedback contains no real participant context.
profiles.surface: Desktop 1440×900; founder evidence panel plus read-only repository review artifact.
profiles.autonomy: Draft a review decision locally. Do not approve a corpus release, publish a comment or alter production data during the session.
profiles.success: Can cite the unsupported relationship or unresolved conflict and record a reason for correction.
profiles.recruitment_proxy: A consenting startup navigator or curator who checks original sources.

profiles.name: Priya
profiles.role: Developer integrating the API and studying GraphRAG
profiles.context: Wants to build a separate interface and reproduce the educational demo without configuring paid services first.
profiles.knowledge: Knows HTTP and JSON. New to this repository. Distinguishes a workflow graph from a knowledge graph once explained.
profiles.goal: Find the fixture quickstart, evidence contract and honest benchmark limitations.
profiles.preferences: Runnable examples, predictable status responses, versioned contracts, and clearly labelled fixture outputs.
profiles.trust: Does not accept a successful website screenshot as proof of standalone API access, secret isolation or graph quality.
profiles.behaviour: Starts from public project documentation, follows the quickstart, and checks whether required credentials or services contradict fixture-only claims.
profiles.frustration: Instructions that require Next.js for an independent API call, undocumented credentials, or mock scores labelled as measured gains.
profiles.disclosure_boundary: Use only disposable local fixture credentials through an authorised test setup. Never paste live keys into a browser, prompt, report or repository.
profiles.surface: Desktop documentation browser; HTTP/CLI companion is separate and only run when the session authorises it.
profiles.autonomy: Read docs and inspect examples. No provisioning, deployment, key rotation or external paid calls.
profiles.success: Can identify how to run fixtures and explain what the report does and does not prove.
profiles.recruitment_proxy: A developer unfamiliar with the repository, attempting the quickstart independently.

profiles.name: Taylor
profiles.role: Founder using keyboard navigation and zoom
profiles.relationship: Testing variant of P2/P3; not a new core market persona
profiles.context: Needs a short prerequisite route and sources while using keyboard input and enlarged content.
profiles.knowledge: Comfortable with forms and research; does not know this interface or keyboard shortcuts unique to it.
profiles.goal: Complete the same core route and evidence task without pointer-only interactions.
profiles.preferences: Visible focus, stable headings, readable reflow and an equivalent textual route.
profiles.trust: Needs the action reached by focus to match the visible label. No meaning should depend on colour or hovering alone.
profiles.behaviour: Uses Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space and Escape as appropriate. Follows visible labels; does not use DOM clicks to bypass an unreachable control.
profiles.frustration: Focus disappearing into a panel, a source available only by hovering, or a map that requires dragging.
profiles.disclosure_boundary: No diagnosis is assigned. This is an input/display constraint, not an emulation of lived disability or a screen-reader user.
profiles.surface: Desktop 1280×800 CSS viewport, keyboard-only; repeat at actual 200% browser zoom if supported. Record zoom separately from viewport.
profiles.autonomy: May use documented keyboard controls and text alternatives; no pointer rescue during the unassisted attempt.
profiles.success: Can reach and leave the prerequisite/source views, correct context and retain orientation.
profiles.recruitment_proxy: Consenting keyboard and assistive-technology users, with their own setups, for later human testing.

profiles.name: Morgan
profiles.relationship: Testing variant of P1/P3; not a new core market persona
profiles.context: Previously explored an idea-stage route. Now has a prototype and wants to recover work after a service interruption.
profiles.knowledge: Remembers the previous question but not every interface detail. Does not assume the app has durable server memory.
profiles.goal: Correct earlier assumptions, retain a draft during failure, and understand what a fresh session knows.
profiles.preferences: Explicit context ownership, visible old/new answer distinction and clear recovery choices.
profiles.trust: Checks whether a previous answer still applies and whether another session can see the first session's fictional context.
profiles.behaviour: Edits stage before submitting again. On an error, tries one visible recovery control; does not repeatedly spend requests to force an answer.
profiles.frustration: Old recommendations presented as updated, losing entered work, or unclear browser-held versus server-held state.
profiles.disclosure_boundary: Only the synthetic marker is used to probe isolation. No real secrets or personal information.
profiles.surface: Desktop 1366×768; fresh isolated browser context for the second-session check, not merely a new tab.
profiles.autonomy: May change own test draft and inspect a fresh session. No account deletion or other-user access.
profiles.success: Can explain which context produced each answer and recover or stop with an intact draft.
profiles.recruitment_proxy: A consenting returning founder whose goals changed between visits.
